judged_text: Multi-host destination calendar collection is gated on `eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"`, which dynamic multi-user links (user1/user2 booking URLs) never satisfy, even though the TODO this diff removes explicitly named "dynamic collective events" as a case to handle. Dynamic group bookings still create calendar events only on the first user's destination calendar — the requirement the deleted comment acknowledged is silently dropped by this fix.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multi-host destination calendar aggregation is only performed when `isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"` (in `handleNewBooking.ts`: building `teamDestinationCalendars` and then `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). In all other cases, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to just the eventType/organizer calendar (wrapped as a single-element array) and no additional host calendars are added. However, the finding’s stronger claim that “dynamic multi-user links never satisfy COLLECTIVE” and thus are definitely broken cannot be verified from the diff alone (we can’t confirm what `schedulingType` those dynamic URLs produce). This is a real, diff-grounded scope/edge-case concern (behavior only implemented for COLLECTIVE), but not a provable defect solely from the shown changes.
